name: Shopee
tagline: Southeast Asian e-commerce marketplace app where millions of sellers list goods and buyers pay through in-app checkout, vouchers and logistics.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Shopee is free for buyers and monetizes sellers through commissions, ad spend and service fees, so there is no monthly subscription number to quote.

verdictSummary: Shopee is not a feature you can clone, it is a two-sided market with tens of millions of buyers and sellers, plus payments, escrow, vouchers, ratings, returns and courier integrations wrapped around it. An agent can absolutely produce a shop front with a catalog, cart and order table in an afternoon; what it cannot produce is anyone to buy from or sell to. The parts that actually make the app work, price competition from thousands of overlapping sellers, COD and local wallet rails, cheap or free shipping subsidies, dispute handling, are commercial and regulatory problems rather than code problems. The nearest honest personal build is a single-vendor storefront for your own goods, which is a completely different product that happens to look similar. If you want to buy cheap phone cases from strangers, you are buying the network, not the software.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted single-vendor storefront: you list your own products, visitors browse and add to a cart, and orders land in a local database with a simple admin view.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine or small VPS to run it on
Your own product photos and inventory data
A real payment provider account if you ever want to take money, which the build deliberately stubs out
Your own shipping arrangement, no courier API included
whatYouLose: The demand side: no buyers arrive because your storefront exists
The supply side: no competing sellers, so no price floor and no selection
Payments, escrow and COD rails, plus the fraud and chargeback machinery behind them
Voucher and free-shipping subsidies, flash sales, and the ratings history that makes a stranger's listing trustworthy
Logistics integration, tracking, returns and dispute resolution
moatNotes: Liquidity first: buyers show up because sellers are there and sellers stay because buyers are there. Payments and last-mile logistics in Indonesia are the second wall, and neither is a weekend of coding.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody pays Shopee a subscription, which is the point: buyers pay in attention and margin, sellers pay in commissions and ad spend, and both keep doing it because the alternative is finding each other alone. A seller with their own storefront has to buy traffic, run their own payment and COD risk, and convince a stranger to trust an unknown domain with cash. Shopee sells that trust and that traffic bundled with courier pickup and a returns process, and it is priced low enough per transaction that building around it rarely pencils out for small sellers.
notes: The storefront is a weekend; the market is not. The moat is marketplace liquidity plus local payment and logistics rails, neither of which ships in your repo.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted single-vendor storefront. This is NOT a marketplace clone: one seller (me), my own products, no third-party sellers, no buyer accounts.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router and TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling, no component library
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/store.db, schema created on first run
- Zod for input validation
- Local filesystem image uploads to ./public/uploads
- No auth provider: a single admin password read from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, checked server side, stored in an httpOnly signed cookie

Data model:
- products: id, slug, title, description (markdown), price_cents, currency, stock, images (json array of paths), active, created_at
- orders: id, buyer_name, buyer_phone, buyer_address, note, subtotal_cents, status (new | packed | shipped | done | cancelled), created_at
- order_items: id, order_id, product_id, title_snapshot, unit_price_cents, qty

Public side:
- / grid of active products with image, title, price
- /p/[slug] product page with image gallery, markdown description, stock, add to cart
- cart persisted in localStorage, cart drawer with qty edit and remove
- /checkout collects name, phone, address, note, then creates an order server side, decrements stock in a transaction, and shows an order reference. Payment is intentionally out of scope: show "pay on delivery or bank transfer, I will contact you" and record the order as new.

Admin side at /admin, password gated:
- product CRUD with image upload and drag-to-reorder images
- order list with status dropdown and a detail view
- a CSV export of orders

Explicitly out of scope: other sellers, buyer accounts, reviews, chat, vouchers, courier APIs, shipping rate calculation, payment gateways, search ranking, recommendations, analytics, telemetry of any kind.

Deliverables: working app with `npm run dev`, a seed script that inserts 8 fake products, .env.example listing ADMIN_PASSWORD and COOKIE_SECRET, and a README with setup and a blunt note that this handles no money and no shipping.
